task_completion.description: The MGED geometry editor is open and active.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A window titled 'MGED' or showing the BRL-CAD interface is visible in the screenshot.

task_completion.description: The 'moss.g' scene is loaded and 'all.g' is displayed in the wireframe viewport.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The 3D wireframe view shows the outlines of an ellipsoid, torus, box, and wedge.

task_completion.description: The agent interacts with the 'File' menu or 'rt' command to start the raytracer.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The 'File' menu is open with 'Raytrace' selected, or the command 'rt' is typed into the MGED command console.

task_completion.description: A new framebuffer window opens to display the rendered output.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A separate window (often titled 'rt' or 'Framebuffer') appears on the desktop.

task_completion.description: The raytracer completes the render of the moss scene.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The framebuffer window shows a fully shaded/colored image of the moss scene objects (ellipsoid, torus, box, wedge) on a ground plane, rather than just wireframes.

integrity.description: The agent interacted with the MGED GUI or command line rather than displaying a static image file.
integrity.visual_evidence: The mouse cursor is seen navigating menus or the command history shows the 'rt' command being entered.

integrity.description: The agent did not simply open an existing image file using an external viewer.
integrity.visual_evidence: The rendering process is visible within the context of the MGED application or its associated framebuffer tool.

integrity.description: The system shows signs of active computation during the raytrace.
integrity.visual_evidence: Progress text in the MGED console or the gradual filling of the framebuffer window with pixels.

privileged_info_for_vlm: The 'moss.g' scene is a standard BRL-CAD benchmark. The 'rt' command is the internal tool used to invoke the raytracer. The resulting render typically features a green/yellow ground plane and multi-colored geometric primitives. The framebuffer is the standard output window for BRL-CAD renders.
